submitted.rationale: Index 23 (Co0.23Sb0.77) had the highest measured EQE, 0.0343%. That is about 5x the 0.0063% of the trirutile CoSb2O6 composition at index 20. The Co-rich spinel region (index 5) gave a negative EQE. So the best merit is on the Sb-rich side of CoSb2O6.

rejected.reason: Stoichiometric trirutile CoSb2O6: XRD shows the phase is present, but EQE was only 0.0063%
Co-rich Co7Sb2O12 spinel region: negative EQE (-0.0068%)

consultations.verdict: Support: MACE puts trirutile CoSb2O6 on the hull (0 eV/atom). The MEGNet HSE gap of 0.37 eV is a known underestimate for Co d-d systems, so it is not disqualifying. Index 20 (Sb 0.674) is closest to the CoSb2O6 stoichiometry, and its XRD shows a clean rutile-type pattern.

Moderate support: MACE puts the Co7Sb2O12 spinel near the hull (0.03 eV/atom). MEGNet gives it a 1.44 eV gap, well below 3.2 eV, so it absorbs strongly. Trirutile at index 20 scored very poorly, so the Co-rich spinel region at index 5 (Sb 0.22) is worth testing.

Weak support: MEGNet gives CoSb2O4 (Sb 0.667) a 1.93 eV gap. That suggests Sb-rich phases next to trirutile can absorb 3.2 eV light. Index 20 was the only measurement with positive EQE, and the Co-rich spinel came out negative. The GP also points toward the Sb-rich side at index 23.
